plan.rationale: Initial baseline plan with no prior observations. Domains cover standard GEMM tile sizes; block_M {32,64,128}, block_N {64,128}, block_K {32,64}, num_stages {1,2,3}, fixed threads=128, and swizzle=[0] to establish a conventional row-major baseline before exploring serpentine locality. All tiles divide M=4096, N=4096, K=1024. Shared-memory cap set to 32768 bytes, matching the hard portability cap (also within the 8192-49152 range), so the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) must stay under 32KB; larger tiles/stages will be pruned by HiGHS accordingly. Weights are uniform at 1 to avoid biasing traffic, launch count, pipeline depth, or footprint before any simulator feedback. The swizzle reuse term is an untested analytical hypothesis; after feedback we will compare simulated traffic/latency and broaden swizzle to [0,4,8,16] or adjust weights if locality gains are not visible. Validation scope: Mac Metal checks run the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. No global optimality is claimed.

Attempt-00 established a numerical-passing, compiling baseline at block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1, swizzle=0 with simulated_us=470.78 and actual smem 32768 bytes (right at the cap). That baseline could not use swizzle for locality, and its large tile plus stage-1 pipeline is likely conservative on both traffic and pipeline depth. This revision broadens swizzle to [0,4,8,16] to test the serpentine panel reuse hypothesis against same-tile swizzle=0, while keeping block_M/block_N/block_K/num_stages domains unchanged so HiGHS can trade off traffic, launches, pipeline, and footprint under the unchanged 32768-byte cap. Weights remain uniform because there is only one observation and no evidence yet to favor or penalize any single feature; the hypothesis is that swizzle>0 reduces analytic traffic via reuse without increasing shared memory, and that smaller stages/tiles may unlock more stages under the cap. We still treat the panel reuse term as analytical, not measured: next round we will inspect actual simulator traffic/latency and, if locality gains do not materialize, down-weight swizzle-driven traffic or narrow swizzle. Validation scope unchanged: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binaries are not run on GB10, and GB10 values are simulator estimates rather than hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.

Two observations so far. Attempt-00 (block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1, swizzle=0) passed numerical, compiled, and simulated at 470.78 us with 32768 actual smem (exactly at the portability cap). Attempt-01 (block_M=64, block_N=128, block_K=64, num_stages=1, swizzle=16) also passed, compiled, and simulated at 402.23 us with 32768 smem; proxy cost dropped to 5.89 versus 10.93. Both attempts used num_stages=1 because the 32768-byte cap excludes large-tile multi-stage options, so pipeline depth has not yet been meaningfully explored. Domains are kept full (block_M/block_N/block_K/num_stages/swizzle all as allowed) to let HiGHS trade smaller tiles for extra stages within the cap and to keep testing swizzle>0 versus swizzle=0 at matched tile shapes. Swizzle is retained across [0,4,8,16] because the swizzle=16 run produced the lower simulated latency, though the reuse term is still an analytical hypothesis; we will again inspect simulator traffic/latency next round before trusting panel locality. Weights are adjusted modestly: pipeline raised to 1.5 since stage count has so far been pinned to 1 and deeper pipelining is a plausible lever once smaller tiles free smem; footprint lowered to 0.75 because actual smem sat at the cap in both runs, so footprint pressure is already enforced by the hard bound and does not need extra multiplicative weight. Traffic and launches stay at 1 for now to avoid overfitting on two points. The 32768-byte limit matches the hard portability cap and remains within [8192,49152]. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. No global optimality is claimed.

Three numerical-passing, compiling observations: attempt-00 (128x64x64, stages=1, swizzle=0) 470.78 us; attempt-01 (64x128x64, stages=1, swizzle=16) 402.23 us; attempt-02 (64x128x32, stages=2, swizzle=16) 399.54 us. All hit 32768 actual smem exactly at the portability cap, and simulated_dram_mb is identical (16.78) across runs, so the simulator does not show swizzle-driven DRAM savings — the analytical panel-reuse traffic term is not materializing as measured traffic. The only latency gain from attempt-01 to attempt-02 came from halving block_K and doubling stages (traffic down, pipeline deeper), not from swizzle, though swizzle=16 was present in both best runs. Keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] to test whether swizzle>0 helps at matched tile/stage and to disambiguate the confounded evidence; keep all tile/stage domains full so HiGHS can trade tile size for extra stages under the 32KB cap (multi-stage at 64x128x32 fits; larger tiles at stages>1 are pruned by the bound). Adjust weights: raise pipeline to 2 because deeper staging at smaller block_K is the clearest observed lever (attempt-02 best) and stages have been pinned at 1-2 by smem; lower footprint to 0.5 since actual smem sits exactly at the hard cap in every run, so the constraint already enforces footprint pressure and extra weighting only distorts the ranking. Traffic stays 1 since measured DRAM is flat and the analytical term is unreliable; launches stays 1 to avoid overfitting three points. Next hypothesis: at matched tile (64x128x32) compare swizzle=0 vs 16 to see if locality is real; also probe stages=3 with block_K=32 and block_M=32 to test whether deeper pipelining lowers simulated latency further. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. No global optimality is claimed.

Four numerical-passing, compiling observations: attempt-00 (128x64x64, st=1, sw=0) 470.78us; attempt-01 (64x128x64, st=1, sw=16) 402.23us; attempt-02 (64x128x32, st=2, sw=16) 399.54us best; attempt-03 (64x128x32, st=1, sw=16) 408.93us. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB across all runs, so the analytical serpentine-reuse traffic term is NOT materializing as measured traffic; swizzle effect on latency is unconfirmed and confounded with tile/stage changes. The clearest observed lever is block_K=32 with stages=2 (attempt-02 vs attempt-03), consistent with deeper pipelining at smaller block_K. Attempt-03 regressing despite same tile as best suggests stage count matters more than swizzle. Keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] to disambiguate swizzle>0 vs swizzle=0 at matched tile/stage, and keep tile/stage domains full so HiGHS can trade tile size for extra stages under the 32KB cap (multi-stage at 64x128x32 fits; try block_M=32 to unlock stages=3). Weights: pipeline=2 (best lever observed), footprint=0.5 (actual smem pinned at hard 32KB cap in all runs so the constraint already enforces it), traffic=1 (measured DRAM flat, analytic term unreliable), launches=1 (avoid overfitting four points). Shared cap stays 32768, matching the portability cap. Next hypothesis: match tile/stage at 64x128x32/stages=2 and compare swizzle=0 vs 4 vs 8 vs 16; also probe block_M=32 with stages=3 for deeper pipelining. Validation scope: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binaries are not run on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Five numerical-passing, compiling observations, all pinned at 32768 actual smem (hard portability cap). Best is attempt-02 (64x128x32, stages=2, swizzle=16) at 399.54 us; attempt-03 (same tile/config but stages=1) is 408.93 us, and attempt-01/04 (64x128x64, stages=1) are ~402.23 us. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB in every run, so the analytical serpentine panel-reuse traffic term is NOT materializing as measured traffic; swizzle=0 vs 4 vs 8 vs 16 has produced indistinguishable latency at matched tile (attempt-01 vs attempt-04 both 402.23 us for 64x128x64 stages=1). Therefore down-weight traffic from 1 to 0.75 (analytic term unreliable, measured DRAM flat), raise pipeline from 2 to 2.5 as deeper staging at small block_K is the clearest observed lever (attempt-02 best). Keep footprint at 0.5 since the hard cap already enforces it, and launches at 1 to avoid overfitting five points. Keep full tile/stage/swizzle domains so HiGHS can trade smaller block_M for stages=3 under the 32KB cap and still test swizzle at matched tile/stage. Next hypothesis: since block_K=32 with stages=2 beat stages=1 at matched tile, probe block_M=32 (or 64x64x32) with stages=3 to test whether deeper pipelining lowers simulated latency further, and compare swizzle=0 vs 16 at that exact matched configuration; if swizzle still shows no latency or DRAM effect, narrow swizzle toward [0,4] in the next revision. Validation scope: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Six numerical-passing, compiling observations, all pinned at 32768 actual smem (the hard portability cap). Best remains attempt-02/05 (64x128x32, stages=2, swizzle=16 and swizzle=8) at 399.54 us, confirming swizzle 8 vs 16 is indistinguishable at matched tile/stage. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB across every run, so the analytical serpentine panel-reuse traffic term has not materialized as measured traffic; prior probes (attempt-01 vs 04) already showed swizzle=0 and swizzle=8 identical at 402.23 us for 64x128x64 stages=1. Since swizzle=0 vs 16 has not been directly compared at the best config (64x128x32, stages=2), keep swizzle=[0,4,8,16] this round to disambiguate that exact match; if swizzle still shows no effect, narrow to [0] next revision. Keep full tile/stage domains so HiGHS can trade smaller block_M or block_N for stages=3 under the 32KB cap (e.g., 32x64x32 or 64x64x32 at stages=3). Weights carried over from attempt-05: traffic=0.75 (analytic term unreliable, measured DRAM flat), pipeline=2.5 (deeper staging at small block_K is the clearest observed lever, attempt-02/05 vs attempt-03), footprint=0.5 (hard cap already enforces it), launches=1 (avoid overfitting six points). Next hypotheses: (a) matched 64x128x32/stages=2 with swizzle=0 to test locality, and (b) block_M=32 or block_N=64 with block_K=32 and stages=3 to test whether deeper pipelining lowers simulated latency further. Validation scope unchanged: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.

Seven numerical-passing, compiling observations, all with actual smem pinned at 32768 bytes (the hard portability cap). Best remains 64x128x32 with stages=2 (attempt-02 swizzle=16, attempt-05 swizzle=8) at 399.54 us. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB in every run, so the analytical serpentine panel-reuse traffic term has NOT materialized as measured traffic; matched-tile comparisons (attempt-01 vs 04 at 64x128x64 st=1, both 402.23 us; attempt-03 vs 06 at 64x128x32 st=1, both 408.93 us) show swizzle has no measurable latency or DRAM effect. The remaining untested matched comparison is swizzle=0 vs 16 at the best config (64x128x32, stages=2); we keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] one more round so HiGHS can run that disambiguation at the best tile/stage. We keep all tile/stage domains full because the 32KB cap has forced every selection to num_stages 1-2, and no configuration with stages=3 has yet been evaluated; smaller block_M/block_N with block_K=32 could unlock stages=3 within the cap, and deeper staging at small block_K is the clearest observed lever (stages=2 beat stages=1 at 64x128x32). Weights carried from attempts 05-06: traffic down to 0.75 because the analytic reuse term is unreliable and measured DRAM is flat; pipeline 2.5 to prioritize the empirically useful lever; footprint 0.5 because the hard cap already enforces memory pressure and extra weight only distorts ranking; launches 1 to avoid overfitting seven points. If this round again shows no swizzle effect at matched config, narrow swizzle to [0] and shift exploration toward stages=3 tiles. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.
